Resolves #19467

A shallow VDOM flight can carry deeper disjoint roots while protecting only its initiator. Each actual emitted root now has captured-depth protection and independent callback ownership. All returned trees are adopted before settlement; skipped initiators retain unclaimed requests, and retired instances cannot alter reused-ID replacements. A dead carrier cancels live roots with a distinct Error; active roots keep late requests until their own flight settles.

Evidence: L3 (committed paired head `97a162d10a`, renderer `08f43d63b2`, companion draft `#19469`) → L3 required (AC-5 live coherence). No close-target residuals; broader acceptance remains on #17844.

## Deltas from ticket

No substantive scope change. Reply completeness applies to submitted roots. Exact captured instances and merge-entry snapshots fence late outcomes. Emitted roots settle independently; carrier destruction cannot reject them through a parent callback cascade, including after a late write.

RA-1’s prior source additionally rejects the survivor before the held reply, and a late write recreates the carrier edge. Each corrected control passes.

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-10-08T08:58:53Z

## Operator-requested post-merge challenge

I compared base `6e19f6031b` and final head `08f43d63b2` with the same real-instance, held-response diagnostic. The lifecycle blob in merged `fb11d56b24` is byte-identical to that head. This audit tests the operator's original toolbar-plus-one-of-eight intent.

**Asymmetric payload generation survives unchanged.** `TreeBuilder`, `VDomUpdate`, the sparse allowlist expression and collision predicate are unchanged by this PR.

| Case | Both exact sources |
| --- | --- |
| Toolbar depth 1 + one dirty button | One batch: toolbar with eight pruned references, plus one expanded button payload |
| Toolbar depth 2 + one dirty button | One sparse toolbar payload: one expanded button, seven pruned references |
| Toolbar and that button both change while the first response is held | Follow-up batch retains one-button scope; both late changes complete |

The old comment's “self-only” claim was stale. The disjoint design predates this PR: [03b000ae](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/03b000aeb8751f661e2270814bc7c7b9c992f00b) introduced it under #8834; [955d5beb](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/955d5beb8377b5b3a9411b7a8d4ad536177445fc) restored depth>1 sparse expansion.

**The new protection addresses a real missing owner.** In carrier(depth1) → toolbar(depth2, only button0 expanded), the old toolbar is emitted without its own updating flag/depth. A late write to covered button0 starts another flight while that batch is held. The new head registers the toolbar and defers that conflicting write. It also adopts the toolbar vnode before the carrier callback: that callback sees the old toolbar class on the base and the new class on the head.

Two challenges remain:

1. **Conservative concurrency boundary.** In the same sparse batch, untouched button7 is a pruned reference. The base admits its independent flight; the head queues it on the toolbar. Both eventually render correctly. Captured scalar depth is an envelope, not the exact sparse footprint. This establishes additional serialization, not a measured application latency regression or a reason to discard the collision repair.
2. **Reproduced exception-cleanup regression — #19477.** At `VdomLifecycle.mjs:459`, the root leaves `inFlightScopes` before `resolveVdomUpdate()` completes. A throwing registered pre-update callback then bypasses that root's catch cleanup. With a late mutation and promise, the base rejects the promise and performs a second render; the head leaves the promise parked, `needsVdomUpdate=true`, old vnode content and one render. A throwing claimed resolver additionally leaves a registry entry on the head. These are injected callback failures at a consumed lifecycle hook, not an observed Grid outage.

**Disposition:** retain emitted-root protection and all-root adoption; repair exception-safe settlement under #19477. Evaluate finer sparse-scope concurrency separately. Reverting to initiator-only protection would restore the demonstrated overlapping-flight gap.

Evidence boundary: six paired Node diagnostic scenarios using real components/Helper and the existing unit runtime; the response is explicitly held and Main delta application is the unit facade. No browser rendering, installed FM, throughput benchmark or whole-release certification is claimed.

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-10-08T09:30:12Z

## App Worker performance follow-through

Verified 8 October 2026 on Apple M5 Max, macOS/arm64, Chrome 154.0.8037.98. Baseline `6e19f6031b3d7625f16197c7b8064fed0e07083a`; PR head `08f43d63b2c88c58c7a469804b21edc82e663bf9`. Merged lifecycle blob matches the tested head.

### Result

The original asymmetric payload optimization remains. Per-root flight ownership fixes a demonstrated overlapping-update gap. Small updates and the paced stream behaved well in this bounded run; large disjoint batches have a measurable App Worker processing cost. Exception-safe settlement needs the separate repair tracked in [#19477](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19477).

### Clean browser comparison

Four pairs, AB / BA / AB / BA order, eight fresh browser runs. Each run covered six workloads; each workload used one untimed shape/counter validation, 30 warm-up batches and 100 timed batches. Every measured batch changed actual DOM state and had the expected root count. No registration/unregistration diagnostic counter wrapper remained in timed batches.

Numbers below are medians of four per-run medians, milliseconds per batch. “App work” is the sum of synchronous enqueue, collection-body, submit and adoption/settlement windows. It excludes the collection timer wait and most of the VDOM/Main roundtrip. It is instrumented elapsed time on the App Worker, not a CPU profiler reading.

| Workload | Emitted roots | Before App work | After App work |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One dirty child among eight, shallow disjoint form | 2 | 0.30 | 0.35 |
| One dirty child among eight, sparse depth-2 form | 1 | 0.20 | 0.20 |
| 8 separate branches, one dirty leaf each | 17 | 0.68 | 0.83 |
| 32 branches | 65 | 1.25 | 1.55 |
| 128 branches | 257 | 4.10 | 5.25 |

For 257 roots, paired median increases were approximately 1.3, 1.2, 1.2 and 0.3 ms. Per-run App-work p95 ranged 4.3–6.9 ms before and 5.7–7.3 ms after. These are ranges across runs, not confidence intervals.

Most full roundtrip medians remained around 16.7 ms because Main's frame scheduling dominates. This does not establish unchanged App Worker cost. Uncontrolled pauses occurred in the baseline, including a 397.8 ms roundtrip; no max-latency guarantee or cause attribution is made. Earlier pilot data with diagnostic wrappers still installed is retained separately and excluded from this table.

### Sustained input

A separate two-second stream fed a change every 4 ms without awaiting each reply. In every clean trial, both sources:

- accepted 500 inputs;
- settled all 1,000 corresponding promises;
- coalesced the work into 121 acknowledged batches / 242 emitted roots;
- reached the correct final DOM, vnode and App property;
- drained the final input in approximately 15–17 ms.

The stream records counts and drain time. Its CPU cost is not inferred from the preceding closed-loop samples. A global promise-map entry also existed in the example; this run does not prove global queue emptiness or test heap retention.

### Mechanism and bounds

The additional registration is required for correctness, but it populates ancestor maps for every emitted root. Existing unregister code scans all retained ancestor maps; the branch fixture observed 61, 625 and 8,641 outer-map entries visited per batch for 8, 32 and 128 branches. These counters were collected only in the untimed validation batch. The scan is a concrete scaling concern, not proof that it alone caused the entire timing increase. Collection/registration and settlement both contribute.

The 0.1 ms clock resolution limits small-workload comparisons. The browser used dedicated App and VDOM workers with actual Main DOM application, standard frame pacing, and the existing Neural Link fixture. This is a local development-build comparison on one active workstation, not a mobile, SharedWorker/Fleet, heap or worst-case-throughput certificate. Pipeline timing includes submission; it must not be added to the App-work number.

### Architecture challenge

The paired six-scenario diagnostic confirmed:

- Depth 1 keeps eight references in the toolbar plus one separate expanded child payload.
- Depth 2 keeps one expanded child and seven pruned references.
- Late toolbar and child changes still complete through a scoped follow-up batch.
- Registering a deeper co-root blocks a truly overlapping late child update and adopts all returned roots before carrier callbacks.
- A clean child pruned from the sparse payload also waits: scalar depth is a conservative envelope, not exact sparse membership.
- Removing a root from cleanup responsibility before settlement completes loses recovery if a settlement callback throws. This is #19477; it was reproduced with injected callback errors, not an observed production Grid outage.

[Public architecture receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19468#issuecomment-6056405628).
